subject: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart & rate limits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart & next steps

Hi Samir / Priya,

Thanks again for your time today — great discussion and really appreciate the clarity on your PoC goals (real-time customer support summarization, PII redaction, and 95th-percentile latency <200ms for common prompts). Quick recap + next steps below.

Recap:
- PoC target: ingest 100k messages/day, ~10k inference calls/day during business hours; most prompts are short (<=256 tokens), occasional long context up to 2k tokens.
- Security: would like to confirm whether Hosted API satisfies your compliance needs for demo data (non-production) — later we can discuss Private VPC for production with KMS.
- Success metrics: latency, cost per 1k requests, and no data retention beyond request scope for PoC.

Next steps (action items):
1) Attached: Redwood quickstart & sample requests (redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf) — contains step-by-step examples to hit the Hosted API from your environment.
2) Samir: share a small sample dataset (<=500 messages) we can use for the PoC tests.
3) We’ll provision a short-lived evaluation API key and raise default rate limits for your account during the PoC.
4) Schedule a 30-min technical kickoff next week to validate streaming vs non-streaming endpoints — propose Tue 2027-03-16 or Wed 2027-03-17.

Notes on deployment mode: for the PoC the Hosted API is usually the fastest path (no infra setup) and supports streaming + structured outputs. If you need predictable sustained throughput (e.g., sustained >200 tokens/sec or strict region isolation), we can evaluate Dedicated capacity or Private VPC. I’ve copied Aditya who can provide technical limits and sample requests.

Links: Mutual Action Plan (MAP) -> https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FinLytics-MAP

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A couple quick clarifying questions before we kick off:  

1) For the Hosted API, what are the default rate limits and concurrency caps? We expect spiky traffic during business hours; want to make sure the PoC won’t be artificially constrained.
2) Do you support region pinning (we have EU-based customers and want routing to a US region for latency testing is fine for PoC, but production needs EU hosting)?
3) If the PoC looks good, what’s the lift and lead time to move to Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC? Any ballpark SLA or cost guidance for Dedicated (monthly commit)?

We can share the sample dataset by EOD. Prefer Tue 03/16 11:00am PT if that works for your team.

— Samir

Great questions — quick answers below, and Aditya will add technical details / sample requests.

1) Hosted API limits (default/PoC raise):
- Default: 600 requests/minute per account (roughly 10 requests/sec) for non-streaming generation.
- Streaming: 20 concurrent streaming connections by default.
- If you expect sustained spikes above these values during the PoC, we can temporarily raise the quotas for the evaluation window — just tell us the expected peak QPS and concurrency.

2) Region pinning: Hosted API supports regional endpoints and routing (us / eu / apac). For PoC you can use the US region; for production we can pin to EU or deploy Private.

3) Dedicated vs Private (high-level):
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, and higher SLOs. Typical lead time: 2–4 weeks after contract + infra scheduling. Pricing: monthly reserved commit (we’ll provide ballpark once we see expected sustained throughput).
- Private VPC/on-prem: for regulated workloads with KMS/HSM and audit controls. Longer onboarding (4–8 weeks) depending on network & compliance requirements.

PoC kickoff: Tue 2027-03-16 11:00am PT works — sending calendar invite. 

Attachments included again for convenience: redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf and our MAP link.

Best,
Marissa

Hey Samir / Priya — quick technical notes and sample requests to help the PoC. Attaching a small request collection (finlytics-sample-requests.json).

- Endpoints (PoC):
  • Generation (non-streaming): POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  • Streaming (SSE): GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-large&prompt=...
  • Embeddings: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings

- Auth: Bearer API key in Authorization header. We’ll create a short-lived evaluation key scoped to the PoC (no data retention).

- Example curl (non-streaming):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <EVAL_KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-large","prompt":"Summarize conversation","max_tokens":256}'

- Rate limits & burst guidance:
  • Default: 600 req/min per account (configurable for trials).
  • Burst handling: the SDK/retries use exponential backoff; 429 responses include Retry-After header.
  • If you need predictable sustained throughput (e.g., >200 tokens/sec sustained or >10k reqs/day with low tail latency), Dedicated is recommended.

- Monitoring & observability: the Console will show per-key latency/usage, per-route breakdown, and token-level cost. We can add you to a sandbox org so you can see the dashboards during PoC.

- Next step from our side: I’ll provision the eval key and temporarily raise your account limits for the PoC window. Please upload the sample dataset to the MAP folder or reply to this thread with a link.

Let me know if you want a short call during the kickoff to test streaming vs polling endpoints — I can be on the call.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
